title: Business Consultation in UAE
tagline: Plan Your Business Move with Confidence
hero_description:
Starting or growing a business in the UAE involves a wide range of decisions — from choosing the right jurisdiction and licence type to understanding ownership rules, costs, and compliance obligations. Business consultation in UAE is designed to help business owners understand their options before committing to a structure, licence, or jurisdiction.

At Horizon Line, business consultation is not a one-size-fits-all conversation. It is tailored to your business activity, goals, and circumstances, helping you approach the UAE market with a well-informed plan rather than guesswork.

content.text: Business consultation in UAE refers to professional advisory support that helps individuals and companies make informed decisions about setting up, running, or restructuring a business. It typically covers areas such as business structure, jurisdiction (Mainland, Free Zone, or Offshore), licensing requirements, ownership considerations, and general regulatory obligations.

items: First-time entrepreneurs unfamiliar with the UAE business environment
Foreign investors evaluating UAE market entry
Existing businesses considering expansion or restructuring

Business owners who need clarity before committing to a structure

items.question: What is company liquidation?
items.answer: It is the formal legal process of closing a registered business, including settling obligations and cancelling licences and registrations.

items.question: Why is formal liquidation necessary?
items.answer: Without formal liquidation, a company may continue to accrue fees, fines, or compliance obligations even if it is no longer operating.

items.question: Does the liquidation process differ between Mainland and Free Zone companies?
items.answer: Yes, procedures can vary depending on the jurisdiction and relevant authority.

items.question: Is a liquidator always required?
items.answer: This depends on the jurisdiction and company structure; not all liquidations require a formally appointed liquidator.

items.question: How long does company liquidation take?
items.answer: Timelines vary depending on the company's structure, outstanding obligations, and the relevant authority's process.

items.question: What happens to employees during liquidation?
items.answer: Employee-related obligations must generally be addressed as part of the closure process, in line with applicable regulations.

items.question: Can a company be liquidated if it has outstanding debts?
items.answer: Outstanding obligations typically need to be addressed or settled as part of the liquidation process.

items.question: What documents are needed for liquidation?
items.answer: Commonly required documents include the trade licence, company formation documents, shareholder resolution, and identification documents.

items.question: Will I receive confirmation once liquidation is complete?
items.answer: Yes, a licence cancellation or closure certificate is typically issued once the process is finalized.

items.question: Can liquidation be reversed once started?
items.answer: This depends on the stage of the process and relevant authority procedures; it is best discussed early if reconsideration is possible.

items.question: Does liquidation apply to Offshore companies as well?
items.answer: Yes, Offshore companies also require a formal closure process, though procedures differ from Mainland or Free Zone entities.

items.question: What common mistakes should business owners avoid during liquidation?
items.answer: Common issues include failing to settle outstanding obligations, missing required documentation, or not obtaining final closure confirmation.

cta.heading: Get Started with Company Liquidation
cta.text: Closing a business correctly is just as important as setting it up properly. Company liquidation ensures your business is formally and legally closed, helping you avoid unnecessary obligations or complications down the line. Speak with Horizon Line to understand your requirements.
